paragraphs.text: For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
paragraphs.original: Πᾶς γὰρ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐξ ἀνθρώπων λαμβανόμενος ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων καθίσταται τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, ἵνα προσφέρῃ δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίας ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν,
paragraphs.translit: Pas gar archiereus ex anthrōpōn lambanomenos hyper anthrōpōn kathistatai ta pros ton theon, hina prospherē dōra te kai thysias hyper hamartiōn,

paragraphs.text: who can bear gently with the ignorant and erring, for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity;
paragraphs.original: μετριοπαθεῖν δυνάμενος τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσι καὶ πλανωμένοις ἐπεὶ καὶ αὐτὸς περίκειται ἀσθένειαν,
paragraphs.translit: metriopathein dynamenos tois agnoousi kai planōmenois epei kai autos perikeitai astheneian,

paragraphs.text: and by reason thereof is bound, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διʼ αὐτὴν ὀφείλει, καθὼς περὶ τοῦ λαοῦ, οὕτως καὶ περὶ αὑτοῦ προσφέρειν περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai diʼ autēn opheilei, kathōs peri tou laou, houtōs kai peri hautou prospherein peri hamartiōn.

paragraphs.text: And no man taketh the honor unto himself, but when he is called of God, even as was Aaron.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐχ ἑαυτῷ τις λαμβάνει τὴν τιμήν, ἀλλὰ καλούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, καθώσπερ καὶ Ἀαρών.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouch heautō tis lambanei tēn timēn, alla kaloumenos hypo tou theou, kathōsper kai Aarōn.

paragraphs.text: So Christ also glorified not himself to be made a high priest, but he that spake unto him, Thou art my Son, This day have I begotten thee:
paragraphs.original: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐχ ἑαυτὸν ἐδόξασεν γενηθῆναι ἀρχιερέα, ἀλλʼ ὁ λαλήσας πρὸς αὐτόν· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε·
paragraphs.translit: Houtōs kai ho Christos ouch heauton edoxasen genēthēnai archierea, allʼ ho lalēsas pros auton· Hyios mou ei sy, egō sēmeron gegennēka se·

paragraphs.text: as he saith also in another [place,] Thou art a priest for ever After the order of Melchizedek.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει· Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ,
paragraphs.translit: kathōs kai en heterō legei· Sy hiereus eis ton aiōna kata tēn taxin Melchisedek,

paragraphs.text: Who in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and having been heard for his godly fear,
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ δεήσεις τε καὶ ἱκετηρίας πρὸς τὸν δυνάμενον σῴζειν αὐτὸν ἐκ θανάτου μετὰ κραυγῆς ἰσχυρᾶς καὶ δακρύων προσενέγκας καὶ εἰσακουσθεὶς ἀπὸ τῆς εὐλαβείας,
paragraphs.translit: hos en tais hēmerais tēs sarkos autou deēseis te kai hiketērias pros ton dynamenon sōzein auton ek thanatou meta kraugēs ischyras kai dakryōn prosenenkas kai eisakoustheis apo tēs eulabeias,

paragraphs.text: though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered;
paragraphs.original: καίπερ ὢν υἱός, ἔμαθεν ἀφʼ ὧν ἔπαθεν τὴν ὑπακοήν,
paragraphs.translit: kaiper ōn hyios, emathen aphʼ hōn epathen tēn hypakoēn,

paragraphs.text: and having been made perfect, he became unto all them that obey him the author of eternal salvation;
paragraphs.original: καὶ τελειωθεὶς ἐγένετο πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ αἴτιος σωτηρίας αἰωνίου,
paragraphs.translit: kai teleiōtheis egeneto pasin tois hypakouousin autō aitios sōtērias aiōniou,

paragraphs.text: named of God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.
paragraphs.original: προσαγορευθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀρχιερεὺς κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.
paragraphs.translit: prosagoreutheis hypo tou theou archiereus kata tēn taxin Melchisedek.

paragraphs.text: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard of interpretation, seeing ye are become dull of hearing.
paragraphs.original: Περὶ οὗ πολὺς ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος καὶ δυσερμήνευτος λέγειν, ἐπεὶ νωθροὶ γεγόνατε ταῖς ἀκοαῖς·
paragraphs.translit: Peri hou polys hēmin ho logos kai dysermēneutos legein, epei nōthroi gegonate tais akoais·

paragraphs.text: For when by reason of the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need again that some one teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of solid food.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον, πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκειν ὑμᾶς τινὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος, οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar opheilontes einai didaskaloi dia ton chronon, palin chreian echete tou didaskein hymas tina ta stoicheia tēs archēs tōn logiōn tou theou, kai gegonate chreian echontes galaktos, ou stereas trophēs.

paragraphs.text: For every one that partaketh of milk is without experience of the word of righteousness; for he is a babe.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος ἄπειρος λόγου δικαιοσύνης, νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν·
paragraphs.translit: pas gar ho metechōn galaktos apeiros logou dikaiosynēs, nēpios gar estin·

paragraphs.text: But solid food is for fullgrown men, [even] those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.
paragraphs.original: τελείων δέ ἐστιν ἡ στερεὰ τροφή, τῶν διὰ τὴν ἕξιν τὰ αἰσθητήρια γεγυμνασμένα ἐχόντων πρὸς διάκρισιν καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: teleiōn de estin hē sterea trophē, tōn dia tēn hexin ta aisthētēria gegymnasmena echontōn pros diakrisin kalou te kai kakou.
